quadHead: Four ways Costa Rica catches tourists off guard.

quad.title: SJO Airport Pirate-Taxi Cartel
quad.tl: A non-orange "taxi" at SJO arrivals quotes ₡21,000 for a four-minute hop, then either gouges you or detours onto the highway toward accomplices — the real orange Taxi Aeropuerto kiosk is inside the terminal at fixed ₡15,000–₡21,000 fares.

quad.title: The Surf-Lesson Board-Damage Ambush
quad.tl: An unlicensed beach-hustler offers a ₡21,000 lesson on Playa Tamarindo, sends you onto the Langosta rocks with a pre-scratched board, then waves a clipboard "damage fee" demanding ₡100,000 cash for scratches that were already there.

quad.title: The Parque Central Cambista Swap
quad.tl: A whispered "cambio, cambio?" on Parque Central either gouges you 20% on the rate or palms a counterfeit ₡20,000 into your stack during the count — every street money-changer in San José is one of three scams.

quad.title: The Tampered "María" Meter
quad.tl: A red taxi flagged outside a hotel runs a flickering meter that ticks past ₡8,000 in the first minute and hits ₡17,500 on a ride Uber would charge ₡5,000 — then the driver waves a calculator and "splits the difference" so you feel like you agreed.

body: Costa Rica: Tourist Scams is part of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series. Every scam is documented against Costa Rican police and tourism-agency sources — the OIJ (800-8000-645), the Fuerza Pública (911), the Policía Turística and the ICT licensed-operator registry — plus r/CostaRica reports, US Embassy San José security alerts, and verified Tico news. Sourced and re-reported, not recycled.

69 specific scams across San José, Manuel Antonio, Tamarindo, La Fortuna, Monteverde and 6 more towns — the fake park-ranger roadblock on the way to Manuel Antonio, the SJO pirate-taxi cartel, the cambista counterfeit-bill swap, the tampered "María" taxi meter, the surf-lesson board-damage shakedown. The exact scripts, the red flags that give them away, and the Spanish phrases that shut them down, in plain Spanish you can show on your phone — with the steps to file a denuncia if it has already happened.
Scams evolve, so the book is re-researched every year, and the current edition sits in your Kindle library. Built for the traveler who wants to move through Costa Rica relaxed, not braced.
